newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Conseco deal to add to earnings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Conseco deal to add to earnings.

text.p: Conseco Inc chairman Stephen Hilbert said he expects Colonial Penn Life Insurance Co to contribute to the company's 1997 and 1998 earnings even though he expects to achieve few cost savings.
Conseco agreed to acquire Colonial Penn from Leucadia National Corp for $460 million in a deal that is expected to close in the third quarter of 1997.
Hilbert, speaking to Reuters in a telephone interview, said he expects Colonial Penn to add about $0.01 a share to earnings in 1997, despite plans to close late in the year.

Hilbert said he expects Colonial Penn to contribute about $0.03 to $0.04 a share in 1998, excluding gains Conseco might achieve by cross-selling its current products through Colonial Penn's direct response marketing system.
Colonial Penn, probably best known for its television commercials featuring former "Tonight Show" sidekick Ed McMahon, uses direct marketing to sell life insurance products.
In addition to television ads, the company uses direct mail and telephone marketing to generate sales.
Hilbert said he plans to sell Conseco's supplemental health, life, annuity and mutual fund products using Colonial Penn's direct marketing methods.
As a result, he said, he plans to allow Colonial Penn to continue operating the way it is in Philadelphia rather than consolidating it into Conseco.
Therefore, he said, he does not foresee the kind of cost savings that might come in a consolidating deal.
Instead, he said, there might even be a slight increase in costs as Conseco develops new advertising for its other products.
The key to this deal, Hilbert said, was the new distribution channel offered by Colonial Penn.
"This is not a consolidation story," Hilbert said.
Although Conseco had a broad distribution system, using both career and independent agents, he said the company did not have direct marketing experience.
"The one distribution point that we have been aggressively looking for is the right direct marketing company," Hilbert said.

"This is going to give us, again, an opportunity to hit the public and to target our markets as far as which segment of the buying public we want to target by the television ads and also the spokespeople that are delivering the message," he said.
"And we think the people that are in place are outstanding," he added.

Conseco continues to look for additional acquisitions, he said, that would give it more critical mass in its product specialties, such as supplemental health, variable annuities and other life insurance products.
"We've finished our rounding out with the Colonial Penn transaction," Hilbert said.
"But, we're going to be looking for opportunities to just have more critical mass in our chosen markets," he said.
He said he would also consider buying blocks of business in the long-term care and other supplemental health businesses.
